name: Arc suppression coil
summary: An adjustable reactor between neutral and earth tuned to cancel the network capacitive earth-fault current.
description: An arc suppression coil is a reactor connected between the system neutral and earth, tuned so that its inductive current balances the capacitive current that flows during a single phase-to-earth fault. The residual fault current becomes very small, so transient arcing faults often self-extinguish and the network can keep running with a sustained earth fault.

Drawings show an inductor with an adjustment arrow between a transformer or earthing transformer neutral and earth, often with a parallel resistor switched in briefly to help fault location. Automatic tuning controllers and neutral voltage measurement are drawn alongside.

Resonant earthing needs dedicated earth-fault detection, such as transient or admittance-based protection, because fault current is too small for simple overcurrent relays. The symbol does not show the tuning range or the detection method.
readingNotes: An adjustment arrow on the reactor shows tuning capability.
Look for a parallel resistor used for fault location.
distinction: An arc suppression coil cancels capacitive fault current; a neutral earthing resistor limits fault current but does not cancel it.
